exits.clearance: center approach, slope, landing and overhead volume clear

roof_scope: 40-80% each roof; built functional roof modules count, plain roof/paint/shadow do not
scene_design:
Variant design: A stands at the rear RIGHT, a two-storey rounded reclaimed power-station/residential hybrid. A's lower street-facing bow wall genuinely curves down to the ground, with broad curved replaceable armor around a recessed generator/control spine covering approximately40% of the lower facade; a straight recessed door remains visible. The second-storey residence steps back on one side and projects on broad brackets on the other, with a curved deep window bay and a single substantial enclosed service duct around20% of that facade. Short straight service ledges and guardrails at only the recessed base corners visually explain a simple rectangular collision approximation while the rounded ground wall remains apparent. Its roof is a low barrel profile with a long supported ventilation monitor and maintenance strip around half the roof, no solar-panel/tank kit.
B stands at the rear LEFT. Its workshop ground plan is L-shaped, with a wider front work wing and a recessed rear side. A half-area upper house occupies the outer part; use a patched asymmetrical single-pitch roof with a broad supported ventilation dormer and repair/drying canopy covering roughly half of its roof. A visible external stair beside the workshop connects to the house door and terrace; it is residential access, not a third map transition. Show the old workshop structure and differently sourced lightweight upper house as two construction episodes. A low roof service canopy and the upper dwelling purposefully occupy the lower roof, with open terrace space. The scrap stock stays against the workshop side.
C sits along the RIGHT wing nearer the foreground but does not hide the front base. It is a long LOW barrel-roof repair shed with a grounded human door and curved roof ribs, an integrated longitudinal vent hood and supported maintenance cradle occupying around half the roof. BESIDE C on its inward side is a reclaimed compressor / heavy coupling frame of broad cylinders and repaired cast housings, visibly grounded and connected to C; this is nonbuilding machinery. Use a separate solid equipment body and short railing toward the rear-right ramp to form its side enclosure.
LEFT functional transition: B's main grounded workshop roller shutter is the designated rear-left map exit, SHOWN CLOSED with a clear door apron and unobstructed vertical shutter travel; it leads through the workshop into the next rear-left district when raised. No extra freestanding gate on this side, no need to expose B's entire interior. RIGHT functional transition: a clearly visible X-axis-aligned short descending SERVICE RAMP between C and A, leading toward the rear-right edge into an underground service portal integrated with machinery/retaining sides. Its approach from the center, sloping floor, landing and destination mouth must read; not a front-cut tunnel. No machinery in the ramp volume.
Other rear stretches use anchored salvaged transformer bodies / solid scrap storage frames with short fences connecting to the buildings, not a continuous perimeter masonry wall. Front foundation: large layered brick/concrete footings with one broad insulated cooling manifold on the left cut, thick segmented electrical conduit with a sealed coupling on the right; keep original planar cuts and sharp top/bottom corner correspondence. The center is a modest clear dry service court enclosed by these distinct silhouettes, not three detached boxes around a vast empty square.
Form sources: INPUT4 is attachment2, for large rounded architectural shells and a recessed middle / horizontal circulation contrast. INPUT5 is attachment5, for the lived-in external stair, add-on house, varied roof/awning profile and construction layers. Reinterpret both in low two-storey scale.
